correctness.rationale: I reconstructed the classification with the occurrence test that interior runs must be traversed in full. One- and two-run candidates give just the two forbidden unary extensions. In a three-run 010 candidate the middle run has length b or both ends must be singletons and the middle length is <b. At length b the supported outer-exponent pairs are two transposed rectangles, with unique internal minimal gap (min(a,c)+1,min(a,c)+1) if a≠c. A 101 candidate gives exactly the singleton ends with a supported zero-run length other than c. For a four-run 0^i1^j0^k1^h candidate, the entire first three runs lie in its shorter prefix and the last three in its shorter suffix. These force j=b, k=c, h≤b and i≤a (the transposed rectangle can allow (i,c) only if c≤a and i≤c). This also bypasses swapped prefix/suffix descriptions in the frozen four-run case split. A five-run candidate starting with 0 contains both four-run boundary blocks, which force it to occur; starting with 1 it must have singleton ends and both shorter factors occur exactly when its internal runs have lengths c,b,c with c≤a. Six runs cannot have both boundary deletions present, and seven or more retain too many runs. The families are disjoint and their counts sum to b+max(a,c)+1+1_{a>c}. The unary case uses the ambient missing letter, and the three-run case gives the shorter symmetric list. In 0010110100, the absent words 0011 and 1100 have present length-three prefixes and suffixes; the source is palindromic with seven runs and a palindrome cannot have an even run count.
residual_risks: The minor prefix/suffix label swap in the four-run prose does not affect the statement or the boundary-block argument given here. The finite recorded tests do not establish the unrestricted formula by themselves.

evidence: Akagi et al. give an output-sensitive algorithm. 3131fc449d40 handles the more general 0^a1^b0^c1^d0^e pattern but leaves a bounded remainder; a3767ec90631 gives a bound on just the palindromic subset of MAWs.
broader_coverage.reasoning: An algorithm may enumerate every particular input without giving the closed symbolic count or a uniform rigidity theorem. The wider pattern's bounded remainder cannot decide the exact remaining families, and a bound on palindromic MAWs cannot rule out nonpalindromic ones.

evidence: With d=b and e=a, the 3131fc449d40 three-run bridge count is b+max(a,c)−2, precisely frozen families 2 and 3. It leaves the non-bridge remainder bounded but unclassified. The cited 2017 construction gives a₂a₁^ka₂, 0≤k≤n−3, as MAWs of a₂a₁^(n−2)a₂.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Credit the exact bridge implication (in a later-dated record) and the earlier short-word overlap. Neither gives the remaining symmetric exponent and endpoint cases or the universal five-run threshold with a seven-run obstruction.

evidence: Akagi et al. use ordinary contiguous MAWs but their five classes are run-encoding algorithm classes. Mieno et al. and a8201f56b9b0 study MAPWs, whose proper-factor requirement tests the palindrome's interior rather than both length-one-shorter boundaries.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Changing MAW to MAPW changes the property: requiring occurrence of the interior is weaker. The five RLE classes and five explicit families also describe different levels of classification.

checked_sources: Frozen RESULT.md Finding and proof §§3–6; comparison with RLE enumeration and the general five-run bridge result
value.rationale: Reversal closure of the MAW set for a palindrome does not force its elements to be individually palindromic. The minimal-run transition is therefore a natural rigidity question. The five-family description explains why reversal does fix each minimal absence through five runs, and the seven-run counterexample identifies where this need no longer hold. This is a structural result for arbitrarily long words, stronger than checking short palindrome instances.
residual_risks: No classification of seven-run MAWs generally or of nonpalindromic five-run source words is established.
